question: IA
answer:
COMPLIANCE DETERMINATION — Qualification basis for approving an aircraft or article for return to service after a MAJOR ALTERATION (14 CFR, U.S. federal). Source: eCFR, pages fetched 2026-11-23T21:24:37Z.

ANSWER (one line): A major alteration may not be approved for return to service by a mechanic certificate holder acting on the certificate alone. The approval requires an inspection authorization (IA) — or one of the equivalent organizational routes in 43.7(c)/(d)/(e) or 43.17. The IA qualification basis is 14 CFR 65.91(c) (five eligibility elements) plus 65.95(a)(1) (three conditions on the privilege), reached through 43.7(b).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. SCOPE AND READING ADOPTED
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The question ('qualifications for inspection auth regarding major alterations') is ambiguous between two different rules. Both are answered below, but the deliverable is organized around the reading that matters operationally:

  Reading A (adopted): Who is qualified to APPROVE FOR RETURN TO SERVICE an aircraft/article after a major alteration, and what does an IA holder specifically need? -> 43.7(b) + 65.91(c) + 65.95(a)(1).
  Reading B (also answered, section 6): Who may PERFORM a major alteration. -> 43.3, 65.81(a). This is a different privilege from approval and does not confer approval authority.

Jurisdiction assumed: United States, 14 CFR. Aircraft category: Part 91 general aviation is the default case; the Part 121/135 and light-sport variations are called out where they change the answer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE RULE CHAIN — why an IA and not 'just an A&P'
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Step 1 — 43.7(a): 'Except as provided in this section and 43.17, no person, other than the Administrator, may approve an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service after it has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration.' (VERIFIED, fetched text.)

Step 2 — 43.7(b): 'The holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization may approve ... for return to service as provided in Part 65 of this chapter.' (VERIFIED.) Note the rule does NOT say the mechanic certificate alone is sufficient for every alteration; it defers to Part 65.

Step 3 — Part 65 then splits the privilege:
  65.85(a) (airframe rating): a rated mechanic may approve an airframe or related part/appliance after work he performed, supervised, or inspected, '(excluding major repairs and major alterations)'.
  65.87(a) (powerplant rating): same structure, '(excluding major repairs and major alterations)'. (VERIFIED, fetched text.)
  65.81(a): the mechanic's general scope, and the 24-month same-type work condition on supervising or approving return to service.

Step 4 — 65.95(a)(1) is the ONLY paragraph in Part 65 that grants approval-for-return-to-service authority over a major repair or major alteration, and it grants it to the holder of an inspection authorization. That is the pivot of the whole answer.

Narrow exception to note and not over-read: 65.87(b) lets a powerplant-rated mechanic approve return to service after a major repair/alteration on a light-sport special-airworthiness aircraft for products NOT produced under FAA approval, when the work was authorized by and performed per instructions from the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA. (VERIFIED, fetched text.) It does not generalize to standard-category aircraft.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. GATE 1 — IA ELIGIBILITY: 65.91(c), five elements (all five required)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  (c)(1) Holds a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and each in effect for a total of at least 3 YEARS.
        Evidence: certificate with both ratings; issue date history sufficient to show 3 years of tenure on each rating.

  (c)(2) Has been actively engaged, for at least the 2-YEAR period before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR.
        Evidence: employment/engagement records, work orders, employer letters covering the 24 months preceding application. (Distinct from the 3-year tenure in (c)(1) and from the 24-month currency rule in 65.83 — do not conflate the three.)

  (c)(3) Has a fixed base of operations at which the holder may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; the base need not be where the authority is exercised.
        Evidence: stated address of record; change-of-base notification filed with the responsible Flight Standards office (see section 5, condition C4).

  (c)(4) Has available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or appliances.
        Evidence: tool/instrument list, calibrated equipment records, current maintenance manuals, AD/subscription service, technical data access.

  (c)(5) Passes a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43.
        Evidence: FAA IA knowledge test report (pass). This is the element that is explicitly about major alterations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. GATE 2 — PRIVILEGE CONDITIONS: 65.95(a)(1), three conditions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
An IA may inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration made in accordance with Part 43, ONLY IF all three of the following hold:

  C1  The work was a major repair or major alteration MADE IN ACCORDANCE WITH PART 43 (i.e., performed to the performance rules of 43.13 and the data requirements of 43.13(a)/(b)).
  C2  The work was done in accordance with TECHNICAL DATA APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR (e.g., TC/STC data, FAA-approved 337 field-approval data, data approved under an FAA-accepted process). Owner-supplied or unapproved drawings do NOT satisfy this.
  C3  The aircraft is NOT maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121. (Part 121/135 certificate holders approve under their own programs via 43.7(e); a Part 135 aircraft outside an approved program remains eligible.)

  C4 (administrative condition on exercising the privilege): if the IA changes fixed base of operations, the privilege may not be exercised until the responsible Flight Standards office is notified; and the IA must meet the recordkeeping requirements of 43.9/43.11 when exercising the authority. (Confirm paragraph designations against the current 65.95 text — see section 9.)

CRITICAL DISTINCTION: the IA approves the WORK for return to service; the IA does not approve the DATA. If the alteration was accomplished on data not approved by the Administrator, condition C2 fails and the IA must refuse approval; the route is FAA field approval (or STC/TC/PMA data, or DER-approved data under an accepted process). Signing off an unapproved-data major alteration is the single most common 65.95 violation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. GATE 3 — CURRENCY AND DOCUMENTATION (must be true at the moment of signature)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  - IA is unexpired. 65.92: each inspection authorization expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year, or on the date the mechanic certificate is surrendered, suspended, or revoked, whichever occurs first.
  - IA has been renewed. 65.93: biennial renewal requires evidence of recent training/activity within the window stated in the rule. Read the current option list before relying on any one pathway.
  - Mechanic certificate currency. 65.83: the mechanic may not exercise certificate privileges unless, within the preceding 24 MONTHS, the Administrator has found the holder able to do the work, or the holder has served as a mechanic under the certificate and rating for at least 6 months of those 24 months.
  - Records. 43.9(d) / Appendix B to Part 43: each person performing a major repair or major alteration executes FAA Form 337 at least in duplicate; a copy goes to the aircraft owner (and, where 43.17 applies, both the performer and the 43.17 approver execute the form). The IA signs the approval-for-return-to-service block of the 337.
  - Operating prohibition and retention. 91.407(a): no person may operate an aircraft that has undergone maintenance/preventive maintenance/rebuilding/alteration unless it has been approved for return to service by a person authorized under 43.7 and the 43.9/43.11 entry has been made. 91.417(a)(2)(vi): copies of the 43.9(d) forms for each major alteration to airframe and currently installed engines, rotors, propellers, and appliances are retained and transferred with the aircraft on sale.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. ALTERNATIVE APPROVAL ROUTES (43.7(c)-(e), 43.17) — for completeness
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  43.7(c) Repair station certificate holder, as provided in Part 145.
  43.7(d) Manufacturer, for work it performed under 43.3(j); except for minor alterations the work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.
  43.7(e) Air carrier operating certificate holder, or holder of a Part 121 or 135 operating certificate, as provided in Part 121/135.
  43.17  TCCA-licensed Aircraft Maintenance Engineer or TCCA-approved AMO, for U.S.-registered aircraft located in Canada — with the express limit that an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer may NOT approve a major repair or major alteration; a TCCA AMO may, if the work was performed in accordance with technical data approved by the FAA. (VERIFIED, fetched text.)
  43.7(f)/(h) Private pilot / sport pilot: preventive maintenance only, not applicable to major alterations.
  43.7(g) Repairman certificate (light-sport) with maintenance rating: LSA only.

Reading B (who may PERFORM): 43.3 permits the holder of a mechanic certificate to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations as provided in Part 65; 65.81(a) excludes major alterations of propellers and any repair/alteration of instruments. Performing a major alteration never carries with it the authority to approve it for return to service.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. DECISION PROCEDURE (apply in order; stop at the first 'no')
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Gate 1  Is the work a major alteration? Classify under 43.3 (affects weight/balance/structural strength/performance/powerplant operation/flight characteristics, or not done per accepted practices/elementary operations) and Appendix A to Part 43.
  Gate 2  Is the signer authorized at all under 43.7? If the only credential is a mechanic certificate, STOP — 65.85(a)/65.87(a) exclude major repairs and major alterations (except the 65.87(b) LSA case).
  Gate 3  If relying on an IA, do all five 65.91(c) elements hold? If any fails, no authority.
  Gate 4  Do all three 65.95(a)(1) conditions hold (C1 Part 43 compliance, C2 Administrator-approved technical data, C3 not a Part 121 continuous airworthiness aircraft)? If C2 fails, refer to FAA for field approval rather than signing.
  Gate 5  Is the IA unexpired and renewed (65.92/65.93), is the mechanic certificate current (65.83), and has the fixed-base notification been made if the base changed (C4)?
  Gate 6  Documentation: Form 337 executed at least in duplicate by each person performing the major repair/alteration (43.9(d)); approval-for-return-to-service block signed by the authorized person; copy to owner; 91.417(a)(2)(vi) retention; 91.407(a) operating restriction lifted only on a valid approval.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
8. AUDIT / NON-CONFORMITY CHECKLIST (most frequent failures)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
  - A&P signs off a major alteration with no IA. Violates 65.85(a)/65.87(a).
  - IA approves work accomplished on unapproved data. Violates 65.95(a)(1) condition C2.
  - IA approves a major alteration on an aircraft in a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program. Violates C3.
  - Form 337 missing, single-copy only, or approval block signed by a person who did not hold a current IA on the signature date.
  - IA operating on an expired authorization (65.92) or without evidence of renewal (65.93).
  - Fixed base changed with no notification to the responsible Flight Standards office before exercising the privilege.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
